messages:
maria: Customer on iOS v2.3.1 sees intermittent 401 invalid_api_key right after SSO sign-in. Happens ~10-30s after login, several users. Repro steps attached.

sam: Thanks — do we know if this is Hosted vs Dedicated? Any org-level SSO provisioning?

maria: Hosted. SSO via our OIDC pipeline (Auth0). Not org-scoped keys — uses short-lived session tokens. Happens across multiple orgs.

jonah: Can you paste the request/response example when it happens? Need full auth header + server log lines (redact actual keys).

maria: Pasting minimal repro (sanitized):
```bash
# client refresh flow (mobile)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/session/refresh \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <refresh_token>" \n  -H "X-Client: mobile-ios/2.3.1" \n  -d '{"device_id":"abc123"}'
```
Response when failing:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_api_key", "message": "refresh token invalid or expired" }

Server log snippet (timestamps are seconds):
```
[2026-06-22T14:12:03Z] session: refresh start user=42 token_id=ft-AAA
[2026-06-22T14:12:03Z] session: refresh start user=42 token_id=ft-AAA
[2026-06-22T14:12:03Z] session: refresh accepted user=42 new_token=st-BBB revoke_old=true
[2026-06-22T14:12:03Z] session: refresh failed user=42 token_id=ft-AAA err=invalid_api_key
```
Looks like two refresh requests hit at the same second.

oncall-eng: That log pattern screams race: two parallel refresh calls with same refresh token. Our refresh handler currently marks old refresh token revoked immediately after issuing a new one, so the second concurrent attempt sees it as revoked and returns 401.

sam: Is this caused by the mobile app doing double-requests? Could be background refresh + foreground. Any way to confirm from client telemetry?

maria: App analytics show two refresh calls for ~15% of users within <200ms after login: background sync triggers + the onResume trigger.

jonah: Short-term workaround: tell support to ask customers to kill background sync (not ideal) or ship an app hotfix to debounce refresh calls. Long-term: make refresh endpoint idempotent for a short window (allow same refresh_token to succeed once and return same new token).

oncall-eng: We can implement a 500ms coalescing window on the server side: when we see a refresh token used, mark it "pending" for 500ms and any concurrent requests return the same new session token instead of revoking. That avoids replay 401s. I'll open an engineering ticket.

support-bot: :ticket: Created TASK-4451: session refresh race coalescing (priority P1), assigned to jonah.

jonah: I'll prototype a fix in the session service:
```go
// pseudo
if entry := cache.Get(refreshToken); entry != nil && entry.Status=="pending" {
  return entry.Issue
}
issueNewToken(refreshToken)
cache.Set(refreshToken, {Status:"pending", Issue: newToken}, 500ms)
```
This returns same newToken to concurrent callers.

sam: Any impact to security/rollback? We must ensure replay window doesn't allow reuse after long time. 500ms looks safe. Also add audit log tag so we can detect coalesced hits.

jonah: Agreed. Will add audit flag and tests.

maria: Can we patch production quickly? Customers have multiple orgs affected.

jonah: Plan: land patch in canary region in 2 hours, monitor for 401 spike drop. If green, roll global in next 4 hours.

support-bot: :white_check_mark: TASK-4451 updated: canary deploy scheduled 02:00 UTC.

maria: FYI customer notified (asked to update to mobile v2.3.2 when available). They appreciate quick turnaround.

oncall-eng: Canary looks good — 401 invalid_api_key events from SSO refresh down 96% in region after canary. Rolling to global now.

sam: Are we also going to ship a client debounce fix?

jonah: Yes, will include a client-side debounce patch in next mobile release (v2.3.2) to avoid hammering refresh endpoint.

maria: Marking resolved for this thread. Will follow up with release notes and support KB: "Why SSO sign-in sometimes returns 401 — mobile refresh race". :memo:

support-bot: Thread closed (resolution: server-side coalescing + client debounce; ticket TASK-4451 closed).
